## Simple explanation

ROUGE is a set of text-comparison metrics often used to evaluate generated
summaries. It checks how much wording or sequences of words overlap with
one or more reference texts.

## Technical explanation

ROUGE variants include n-gram overlap (ROUGE-N), longest common subsequence
(ROUGE-L), and summary-level variants. Scores can be reported as precision,
recall, or F-measure, depending on the implementation. Tokenization,
stemming, aggregation, and reference selection affect results.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

ROUGE provides a reproducible automatic comparison for summarization
experiments. It is inexpensive to compute but does not fully capture
semantic equivalence, factuality, coherence, or usefulness, so it should be
paired with other evaluations.

## How it works

The metric compares tokens or subsequences in a candidate output with
reference summaries. It counts matching units and computes overlap-based
scores. Multiple references can increase the chance that valid wording
choices are represented.

## Practical example

For a summarization model, evaluate generated summaries against human
references with a fixed ROUGE implementation and tokenization. Also inspect
factual errors and human judgments, since a high overlap score can coexist
with unsupported claims.

## Common misconceptions

- ROUGE is not a direct measure of factual correctness or overall summary
  quality.
- Different implementations and preprocessing settings can produce
  different scores, so comparisons require a consistent setup.
